n: Jesus Christ, their advocate, addresses elders met on the Missouri River at Chariton. He understands human weakness and knows how to help those who are tempted.

f.g: Help, come to the aid of.

n: These elders haven’t yet reached Zion, so their mission isn’t complete.
Still, they are blessed: their testimonies are recorded in heaven for angels to see, angels rejoice over them, and their sins are forgiven. Testimony borne is never wasted.
They should continue to Zion, meet together, rejoice, and partake of the sacrament.

f.g: Partake of the Lord’s supper or offer worship.

n: Afterward they may return together or in pairs—it doesn’t matter—only be faithful and share the good news.
The Lord brought them together so the faithful could rejoice together in Missouri. He promises, and he cannot lie.
Anyone who wishes may ride horses, mules, or carriages for the return, as a gift from the Lord received with thanks.
These choices are left to their judgment and the Spirit’s guidance. The Lord trusts their agency.
The kingdom is theirs, and the Lord is always with the faithful.

f.w: I am with the faithful always
